                                                   PUC PROJECT No. 58481
                                                                  §
            Rulemaking to Implement                               §       Public Utility Commission
            Large Load Interconnection                            §
            Standards Under PURA § 37.0561                        §             of Texas


                                                                  Engine 1


                                Engine 1’s Comments on PUCT Staff’s Proposal for Publication

                                                             I.       Introduction
                     Engine 11 submits these comments in response to PUCT Staff’s Proposal for Publication
            filed on February 13, 2026, in the above-captioned project to implement PURA § 37.0561. The
            proposed rule that is approved in this rulemaking proceeding will govern which large load
            customers qualify for Batch Zero and will be incorporated directly into ERCOT’s Planning Guide
            Revision Request (“PGRR”) 145. Given the rule’s immediate and far-reaching consequences for
            large load interconnection, Engine 1 respectfully urges the Commission to address the areas of
            concerns discussed below before approving PUCT Staff’s Proposal for Publication at this
            Thursday’s March 12th open meeting.2


                       II.      Specific Areas of Concern with PUCT Staff’s Proposal for Publication


                                 a. Proposed Subsection(d) – Intermediate Agreement Requirements
                     Proposed Section (d) imposes premature and disproportionate financial obligations at the
            Intermediate Agreement phase, before any interconnection study has begun. Subsection (d)(1)
            requires a large load customer to execute a lease or purchase land for a proposed site at a point
            when no interconnection study has been initiated or completed by the interconnecting distribution
            service provider (“DSP”), transmission service provider (“TSP”), or ERCOT. The Commission
            should permit a broader range of site-control instruments at this phase, including Purchase and

            reindustrialization in the United States.
            2
             See PUCT Staff’s Memo and Proposal for Publication for consideration at the February 20, 2026, Open Meeting,
            Project No. 58481 (February 13, 2026).


                                                                      1
 Docusign Envelope ID: 7C1B97C4-6E4C-444A-98EE-6818E574A098




            Sale Agreements, Options to Purchase, Rights of First Refusal, Rights of First Offer, and
            Exclusivity Agreements. In addition, the per-MW financial security deposits required by
            Subsections (d)(10) and (d)(11) are premature and excessive at this phase when a large load
            customer has no confirmed interconnection path. Financial security at the Intermediate Agreement
            phase should be limited to actual costs incurred on the large load customer’s behalf by an
            interconnecting DSP or TSP. Any financial security posted at the Intermediate Agreement phase
            should be fully refunded to the large load customer upon withdrawal of its interconnection request,
            net of any outstanding amounts actually owed to the interconnecting DSP or TSP.


                         b. Proposed Subsection (f) – Interconnection Agreement Requirements
                     The non-refundable interconnection fee of $100,000 per MW in proposed Subsection (f)(7)
            is duplicative and should be eliminated. Large load customers are already required to fund 100%
            of their direct interconnection costs through contribution in aid of construction (“CIAC”) and to
            post financial security for long-lead-time equipment and transmission upgrades. An additional per-
            MW fee untethered to any actual cost violates cost-causation principles and imposes an unjustified
            financial burden on large load customers. Furthermore, applying this fee as an offset to a TSP’s
            rate base risks over-collection of revenue and creates unnecessary ratemaking complexity; a
            minimum demand charge in the TSP’s tariff would be a more appropriate and transparent
            mechanism.


                         c. Proposed Subsections (d)(10) and (d)(11) and Subsections (f)(7) and (f)(8) –
                            Financial Commitments at Intermediate and Interconnection Agreement
                            Phase


                     The proposed rule creates a compounding financial security burden that should be clarified
            or restructured. At the Intermediate Agreement phase, Subsections (d)(10) and (d)(11) require
            financial security of $100,000 per MW of requested peak demand plus additional security for long-
            lead-time equipment. At the Interconnection Agreement phase, Subsections (f)(7) and (f)(8)
            require payment of a non-refundable interconnection fee of $100,000 per MW of contracted peak
            demand plus further financial security for long-lead-time equipment. A plain reading of the
            proposed rule requires cumulative financial security of up to $200,000 per MW across both phases.
            The Commission should clarify whether financial security posted at the Intermediate Agreement


                                                             2
 Docusign Envelope ID: 7C1B97C4-6E4C-444A-98EE-6818E574A098




            phase carries over and offsets obligations at the Interconnection Agreement phase, so that large
            load customers have certainty about their total financial exposure at each step in the
            interconnection process.


                         d. Proposed Subsection (g)(3) and (4) and Subsection (h)(3) and (4) – 80/20%
                            Refund Split for Withdrawals and Underutilized Capacity

                     The 80/20% refund split between the interconnecting TSP and a large load customer in
            proposed Subsection (g)(3) and (4) that applies when a large load customer withdraws all or a
            portion of its requested or contracted peak demand and proposed subsection (h)(3) and (4) that
            applies when a large load customer fails to meet a milestone in its energization schedule is unfair,
            not based on cost causation principles, and an unnecessary penalty on large load customers. Once
            a TSP has applied a large load customer’s financial security to all outstanding amounts owed, the
            remaining balance should be fully refunded back to a large load customer. Permitting the TSP to
            retain 80% of that surplus as a rate-base offset is a windfall that bears no relationship to any costs
            incurred on the large load customer’s behalf by an interconnecting TSP. The Commission should
            require the TSP to refund 100% of the unspent balance after all outstanding amounts are satisfied.
            Allowing TSPs to capture residual financial security amounts as a revenue stream would create
            perverse incentives and an unfair penalty incompatible with the Commission’s cost-causation
            obligations.

                                 e. Long-Lead-Time Equipment Paid for by Large Load Customers

                     A large load customer that has fully funded long-lead-time equipment should retain
            ownership and the right to redeploy that equipment at an alternative site location. Where a large
            load customer has paid in full for such equipment, the proposed rule should be amended to vest
            title in the large load customer rather than the interconnecting DSP or TSP. Denying a large laod
            customer the right to redeploy equipment it has entirely funded is unjust and creates a significant
            disincentive to early procurement of critical materials.


                                                             III.   Conclusion
                     Engine 1 respectfully urges the Commission to address the concerns identified above
            before approving PUCT Staff’s Proposal for Publication. Engine 1’s proposed changes are


                                                                    3
 Docusign Envelope ID: 7C1B97C4-6E4C-444A-98EE-6818E574A098




            narrowly targeted, grounded in cost-causation principles, and necessary to ensure the rule operates
            fairly and predictably for large load customers navigating the Batch Zero and ongoing batch study
            interconnection process.




            Respectfully submitted,




            Adam Taylor
            Chief Development Officer
            Engine No. 1 ATA Power
